::: {.subtitle}
Postdoctoral Fellow · Department of Biology, Emory University
:::

::: {.lede}
I develop and apply computational methods to understand how pathogens generate
genetic diversity, move between host species, and spread through populations.
:::

I am currently a postdoctoral fellow in the Katia Koelle lab at Emory
University. Before that I was a postdoc with Louise Moncla at the University of
Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine, and I completed my PhD in
bioinformatics at the University of Georgia with Justin Bahl, as an NSF NRT
fellow in Interdisciplinary Disease Ecology Across Scales.

## Research interests

- Phylodynamics and scalable Bayesian inference for genomic surveillance
- Reassortment and diversification in segmented viruses
- Multi-host transmission and spillover, particularly avian influenza H5N1
- Within-host viral evolution in prolonged and chronic infections
- Antigenic evolution of seasonal influenza

## Teaching

I lecture on phylogenetics, phylodynamics, and molecular epidemiology, for
audiences ranging from undergraduates to practicing public health scientists. I
think understanding the theory behind a method makes for better application and
troubleshooting, so I write practical material that lets students test what
they have just heard in lecture rather than only read about it. Those materials
are collected under [Teaching resources](teaching.qmd).
